# HSLU OrbbecStreamer

- [Introduction](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs): Stream live RGB-D from Orbbec cameras to the browser, GPU-encoded end to end.
- Getting Started
  - [Install the server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/getting-started/install-server): The shortest path to a built server, linking out to the full server documentation for every detail.
  - [First stream](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/getting-started/first-stream): Capture your own camera through the full server pipeline today; stream it to a browser once serving lands.
- Guides
  - [Calibration](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/calibration): What each calibration kind does, what works today on the server and the client, and why they can't yet be chained into one flow.
  - [Placement](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/guides/placement): Move a server's point cloud into position and commit it, and what happens on the server side today.
- Server
  - [Server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server): The C++/CUDA server that captures, encodes and streams Orbbec camera data.
  - [Requirements](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/requirements): The hardware, operating system, drivers and SDKs the server needs, and how to check each one.
  - [Install](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/install): Install the system packages, CUDA, TensorRT, the Orbbec SDK and vcpkg, and optionally build the RVM segmentation engine.
  - [Build and test](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/build): Configure and build the server with the CMake presets or the Makefile, and run the unit, integration, smoke and hardware tests.
  - [Configuration](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/configuration): The live YAML config file, every option it accepts, and how to check a config before you run it.
  - [Stream layout](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/stream-layout): Choose between concatenated and per-camera encoding, what each produces, and the encoded colour and depth bitstreams.
  - [Run the server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/running): Start the live capture and encode pipeline, run the hardware checks, stop the server cleanly and fix common start-up failures.
  - [Read the telemetry](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/telemetry): What every periodic log line of the live server means, what healthy numbers look like, and how to act on drops, skew and queueing.
  - [Camera pose calibration](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/camera-calibration): Print the ChArUco board, calibrate where each depth camera sits, and read the calibration state at startup.
  - [Depth quantization calibrator](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/depth-quantization-calibrator): Fit the 10-bit depth code table to your scene with orbbec_streamer_depth_quantization_calibrator.
  - [Serve to browsers](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/serving): Status of the WebTransport server, the TLS certificates browsers need, and how to try the WebTransport spike.
  - How it works
    - [How the server works](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/architecture): The live pipeline from the cameras to the encoded bundles, which thread owns each stage, the bounded queues, the clock domains and what leaves the server today.
    - [Capture and synchronisation](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/capture-and-sync): How the server opens the cameras, synchronises them in hardware and in time, aligns colour to depth and groups frames from all cameras into batches.
    - [GPU processing](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/gpu-processing): How captured frames reach the GPU, how the foreground mask and the bilateral depth filter work, what they cost and where their limits are.
    - [Encoding](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/encoding): How the server encodes colour and depth with NVENC HEVC, its low-delay settings, bitrates, keyframes and encoder sessions.
    - [Latency](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/latency): Where the server's latency comes from, the targets, what the server does to stay out of the way, and what is still planned.
    - [Setup state](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/server/how-it-works/setup-state): The server's setup and readiness model, how it maps to the wire, the revisions, the setup lease, autocalibrate and setup.json.
- Client
  - [Tour of the client](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/tour): Open the client, find each part of its screen, and go from adding a server to the 3D view.
  - [Use the browser client](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client): What the OrbbecStreamer browser client does, what works today, and which page to read for each task.
  - [What you can tweak](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/what-you-can-tweak): Every control in the client, one table per area, with what it changes, its range and default, and when to change it.
  - [Run the client](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/dev-build): Install the browser client, start it on your machine and open it in your browser.
  - [Check your browser](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/browser-requirements): Find out whether your browser can connect, decode and draw point clouds, and what the client does when it can't.
  - [Add a server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/add-a-server): Connect the client to a capture server by its address, or add the built-in mock server to try the client without hardware.
  - [Read a server card](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/server-card): What each part of a server card means, what its buttons do, and how to fix a refused lock, stale data or a lost connection.
  - [Move around the 3D view](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/viewer): What the 3D view shows, how to orbit, pan and zoom, how overlapping cameras are blended, and what to do when nothing is drawn.
  - [Play a recording](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/playback): Play a recorded colour and depth video pair in the client, without a server or a camera.
  - [Set up a server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/setup-workspace): Open the setup view for one server, hold its setup lock while you calibrate or place it, and leave again.
  - [Calibrate depth](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/calibration): Run a depth-quantization calibration from the setup view, watch its progress, and commit or cancel the result.
  - [Place a server in the scene](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/placement-editing): Move a server's point cloud into position with numbers or a 3D handle, then commit the placement so every client sees it.
  - [Move an anchor in your view](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/world-anchors): Move where your browser draws an anchor, and every server placed relative to it, without changing anything on the servers.
  - Developer
    - [Test the client](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/test-the-client): Run the client's type check, unit tests and build, open the dev check pages, and see which browsers have been tested.
    - [Mock server](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/mock-server): A deterministic in-process capture server for client tests and dev pages.
    - [Contract gaps and interim behaviour](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/interim-behaviour): Where the protocol contract is still open, what the client does in the meantime, and what the mock server assumes.
    - [Developer options](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/developer-options): Renderer settings, connection timing and fixed intervals that have no control in the client UI, with their defaults and where to set them.
    - [Cards check](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/cards-check): A dev page that runs two clients of one mock server side by side and drives their server cards through a scripted scenario.
    - [Setup check](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/setup-check): A dev page that drives the setup workspace through a scripted depth-quantization calibration against one mock server, with a second client watching.
    - [Placement check](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/placement-check): A dev page that drives placement editing and world anchors through a scripted scenario with two clients of one mock server.
    - [Latency measurement](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/client/developer/latency): Measure where the client spends time between the network and the screen, in the browser and in Node.
- [Troubleshooting & FAQ](https://irc-hslu.github.io/orbbecstreamer/docs/troubleshooting-faq): Cross-team questions and where to find every build and run failure.
